title: Does ex(n, G_k) = o(n^{3/2}) for any k >= 4

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in graph theory: Does ex(n, G_k) = o(n^{3/2}) for any k >= 4.

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEY+FORMALIZATION: Created OQ-01 formalization. Established logical hierarchy and key bounds. Problem open for k≥4. 2 axioms (known results), 4 sorries.
builtItems: Created Erdos1021OQ01.lean with 8 theorems, 2 axioms, 4 sorries
Defined weakConjectureK4 = ∀ k ≥ 4, isLittleO (exGk k) n^{3/2}
Proved O(n^{3/2}) ≠ o(n^{3/2}) (separating trivial bound from the question)
Proved lower bound exponent < 3/2 and approaches 3/2 as k→∞
insights: OQ-01 asks: for k≥4, does ex(n,G_k) = o(n^{3/2})?
k=3 is settled: G_3=C_6, ex(n,C_6) ≪ n^{7/6} (Bondy-Simonovits)
KST trivial bound: ex(n,G_k) ≤ C·n^{3/2} (because G_k contains K_{2,C(k,2)})
O(n^{3/2}) ≠ o(n^{3/2}): KST alone insufficient to resolve OQ-01
Problem is harder for larger k: lower bound exponent approaches 3/2
Both strong and weak forms open for ALL k ≥ 4
